newsitem.title: UK: Stocks lower around the world.
newsitem.headline: Stocks lower around the world.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Wednesday.

LONDON - A weak opening on Wall Street and worries about higher U.S. and British interest rates dragged the British stock market down. The FTSE 100 share index closed a lackluster trading session 16.6 points lower at 3,955.7, just off the day's lows. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down eight points at the time.

FRANKFURT - German stocks eased slightly in market trade, their pace checked a bit by overnight weakness on Wall Street, but they were still resiliant after the recent run-up to record levels. The 30-stock DAX index ended down 2.38 points at 2,625.70 after hovering in a six-point range throughout the session. In after-hours trading, the index stood at 2,621.20, down 5.23.

PARIS - The French stock market showed little reaction to the French 1997 budget unveiled Wednesday and closed slightly lower as it digested recent gains. "The market is consolidating calmly. The budget conformed to expectations," a trader said. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 8.13 points, or 0.39 percent, at 2,072.73.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended a volatile day virtually unchanged while investors concentrated on banking group Swiss Bank Corp. (SBC). SBC added 4.75 francs ($3.83), or 2.01 percent, to end at 241.50 francs ($194.57) after announcing a restructuring of its domestic operations. The measures include 1,700 job cuts and write-offs totalling 3.3 billion francs ($2.7 billion). SBC also forecast a 1996 loss of 1.9 billion francs $1.5 billion).
The all-share Swiss Performance Index lost 1.25 points, or 0.05 percent, to end at 2,365.47.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks were dealt a setback Wednesday as profit-talking emerged to send the key Nikkei average down after big gains over the last two trading days. But brokers said that the index is likely to be supported at around 21,000 where investors' buying is said to be positioned. The key Nikkei 225 average closed down 153.84 points at 21,156.75.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index closed modestly easier, off lows but just below its important resistance level of 11,600, as profit-takers and bulls struggled to dictate the market's direction, brokers said. The Hang Seng Index closed down 27.58 points at 11,594.03 after dipping as much as 95 points down during the day.

SYDNEY - The Australian share market slipped further in late trading on continuing concerns about the direction of metal prices and emerging bearish sentiment toward industrial shares. The All Ordinaries index closed 19.30 points lower at 2,235.10.

JOHANNESBURG - South African stocks' run-up of the past two days was halted with stocks toppling off their high levels on profit-taking and other factors. The industrial index lost 56.5 points to 8,155.2, dragging down the the overall index 36.0 points to 6,911.1. Gold shares took a knock, uninspired by bullion's hold on the $383 level, dealers said. The gold index ended 20.2 points lower, or more than 1 percent, at 1,756.3.
